verses.greek: Καὶ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ γάμος ἐγένετο ἐν Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ ἦν ἡ μήτηρ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐκεῖ·
verses.dgt: And on the third day there was a wedding in Cana of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there.
verses.literal: And on the day the third a wedding came-to-be in Cana of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there.
notes: John’s “third day” language is retained directly.

verses.greek: ἐκλήθη δὲ καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν γάμον.
verses.dgt: Jesus also was invited to the wedding, along with his disciples.
verses.literal: And also Jesus and his disciples were invited to the wedding.

verses.greek: καὶ ὑστερήσαντος οἴνου λέγει ἡ μήτηρ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ πρὸς αὐτόν· Οἶνον οὐκ ἔχουσιν.
verses.dgt: And when the wine ran short, the mother of Jesus said to him, “They have no wine.”
verses.literal: And wine having fallen short, the mother of Jesus says to him, Wine they do not have.
notes: ὑστερέω has the sense of lacking or falling short; DGT uses “ran short.”

verses.greek: καὶ λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί, γύναι; οὔπω ἥκει ἡ ὥρα μου.
verses.dgt: And Jesus said to her, “What is that to me and to you, woman? My hour has not yet come.”
verses.literal: And Jesus says to her, What to me and to you, woman? Not yet has come my hour.
notes: Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί is a difficult Semitic-style idiom. DGT deliberately keeps its foreign shape rather than smoothing it away.
γύναι (“woman”) is not inherently rude in Greek, though it sounds less intimate than “mother” in English.
“My hour” becomes an important Johannine motif.

verses.greek: λέγει ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ τοῖς διακόνοις· Ὅ τι ἂν λέγῃ ὑμῖν ποιήσατε.
verses.dgt: His mother said to the servants, “Whatever he tells you, do it.”
verses.literal: His mother says to the servants, Whatever he may say to you, do.

verses.greek: ἦσαν δὲ ἐκεῖ λίθιναι ὑδρίαι ἓξ κατὰ τὸν καθαρισμὸν τῶν Ἰουδαίων κείμεναι, χωροῦσαι ἀνὰ μετρητὰς δύο ἢ τρεῖς.
verses.dgt: Now there were six stone water jars standing there, according to the purification practice of the Jews, each holding two or three measures.
verses.literal: And there were there stone water-jars six, according to the purification of the Jews, lying there, holding each measures two or three.
notes: A μετρητής was roughly 39 litres; DGT retains the ancient measure in the translation.

verses.greek: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Γεμίσατε τὰς ὑδρίας ὕδατος· καὶ ἐγέμισαν αὐτὰς ἕως ἄνω.
verses.dgt: Jesus said to them, “Fill the water jars with water.” And they filled them to the top.
verses.literal: Jesus says to them, Fill the water-jars with water; and they filled them up to the top.

verses.greek: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἀντλήσατε νῦν καὶ φέρετε τῷ ἀρχιτρικλίνῳ· οἱ δὲ ἤνεγκαν.
verses.dgt: And he said to them, “Now draw some out and take it to the master of the banquet.” So they took it.
verses.literal: And he says to them, Draw now and carry to the master-of-the-banquet; and they carried it.
notes: ἀρχιτρίκλινος is the banquet-master or master of ceremonies.

verses.greek: ὡς δὲ ἐγεύσατο ὁ ἀρχιτρίκλινος τὸ ὕδωρ οἶνον γεγενημένον, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδει πόθεν ἐστίν, οἱ δὲ διάκονοι ᾔδεισαν οἱ ἠντληκότες τὸ ὕδωρ, φωνεῖ τὸν νυμφίον ὁ ἀρχιτρίκλινος
verses.dgt: When the master of the banquet tasted the water that had become wine—and he did not know where it came from, though the servants who had drawn the water knew—the master of the banquet called the bridegroom
verses.literal: And when the master-of-the-banquet tasted the water having become wine, and did not know from where it is, but the servants knew, the ones having drawn the water, the master-of-the-banquet calls the bridegroom

verses.greek: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Πᾶς ἄνθρωπος πρῶτον τὸν καλὸν οἶνον τίθησιν, καὶ ὅταν μεθυσθῶσιν τὸν ἐλάσσω· σὺ τετήρηκας τὸν καλὸν οἶνον ἕως ἄρτι.
verses.dgt: and said to him, “Everyone serves the good wine first, and when they have drunk freely, the inferior. You have kept the good wine until now.”
verses.literal: and says to him, Every person first the good wine sets out, and whenever they have drunk freely, the inferior; you have kept the good wine until now.
notes: The verb μεθύσκω can imply becoming drunk/intoxicated; “have drunk freely” preserves the sense without over-translating the social setting.

verses.greek: ταύτην ἐποίησεν ἀρχὴν τῶν σημείων ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ ἐφανέρωσεν τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.
verses.dgt: Jesus did this, the beginning of his signs, in Cana of Galilee, and revealed his glory, and his disciples believed in him.
verses.literal: This Jesus did as beginning of the signs in Cana of Galilee and revealed his glory, and his disciples believed into him.
notes: John calls this the “beginning of the signs” (ἀρχὴ τῶν σημείων), not simply the first miracle.

verses.greek: Μετὰ τοῦτο κατέβη εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ αὐτὸς καὶ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐκεῖ ἔμειναν οὐ πολλὰς ἡμέρας.
verses.dgt: After this he went down to Capernaum—he and his mother and his brothers and his disciples—and they remained there not many days.
verses.literal: After this he went down to Capernaum, he and his mother and his brothers and his disciples, and there they remained not many days.
notes: μένω (“remain/stay”) is characteristic Johannine vocabulary.

verses.greek: Καὶ ἐγγὺς ἦν τὸ πάσχα τῶν Ἰουδαίων, καὶ ἀνέβη εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ὁ Ἰησοῦς.
verses.dgt: Now the Passover of the Jews was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
verses.literal: And near was the Passover of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
notes: John explicitly calls it “the Passover of the Jews.”

verses.greek: καὶ εὗρεν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ τοὺς πωλοῦντας βόας καὶ πρόβατα καὶ περιστερὰς καὶ τοὺς κερματιστὰς καθημένους,
verses.dgt: And in the temple he found those selling cattle and sheep and doves, and the money changers sitting there.
verses.literal: And he found in the temple the ones selling cattle and sheep and doves and the money-changers sitting,
notes: ἱερόν refers to the larger temple complex; verse 19 uses ναός for the sanctuary/temple proper.

verses.greek: καὶ ποιήσας φραγέλλιον ἐκ σχοινίων πάντας ἐξέβαλεν ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ τά τε πρόβατα καὶ τοὺς βόας, καὶ τῶν κολλυβιστῶν ἐξέχεεν τὰ κέρματα καὶ τὰς τραπέζας ἀνέστρεψεν,
verses.dgt: And making a whip from cords, he drove them all out of the temple, both the sheep and the cattle; and he poured out the coins of the money changers and overturned their tables.
verses.literal: and having made a whip from cords, all he drove out from the temple, both the sheep and the cattle, and of the money changers he poured out the coins and the tables overturned.
notes: The wording does not require the conclusion that Jesus struck people with the whip; sheep and cattle are explicitly mentioned.

verses.greek: καὶ τοῖς τὰς περιστερὰς πωλοῦσιν εἶπεν· Ἄρατε ταῦτα ἐντεῦθεν, μὴ ποιεῖτε τὸν οἶκον τοῦ πατρός μου οἶκον ἐμπορίου.
verses.dgt: And to those selling the doves he said, “Take these things away from here! Do not make my Father’s house a house of commerce.”
verses.literal: And to the ones selling the doves he said, Take these things from here; do not make the house of my Father a house of commerce.
notes: οἶκον ἐμπορίου is literally a “house of commerce/trade.”

verses.greek: ἐμνήσθησαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι γεγραμμένον ἐστίν· Ὁ ζῆλος τοῦ οἴκου σου καταφάγεταί με.
verses.dgt: His disciples remembered that it is written, “Zeal for your house will consume me.”
verses.literal: His disciples remembered that it is written, The zeal of your house will consume me.
notes: The quotation uses the future: “will consume me.”

verses.greek: ἀπεκρίθησαν οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Τί σημεῖον δεικνύεις ἡμῖν, ὅτι ταῦτα ποιεῖς;
verses.dgt: So the Jews responded and said to him, “What sign do you show us, since you are doing these things?”
verses.literal: Therefore the Jews answered and said to him, What sign do you show to us, because these things you do?
notes: ὅτι can carry a causal sense here: they demand authorization for doing these things.

verses.greek: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Λύσατε τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον καὶ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερῶ αὐτόν.
verses.dgt: Jesus answered and said to them, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”
verses.literal: Jesus answered and said to them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it.
notes: The imperative “Destroy this temple” can function as a challenge/condition, not necessarily a command expressing Jesus’ desire.

verses.greek: εἶπαν οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι· Τεσσεράκοντα καὶ ἓξ ἔτεσιν οἰκοδομήθη ὁ ναὸς οὗτος, καὶ σὺ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερεῖς αὐτόν;
verses.dgt: So the Jews said, “This temple was built over forty-six years, and you will raise it up in three days?”
verses.literal: Therefore the Jews said, In forty-six years this temple was built, and you in three days will raise it?
notes: The Greek says the temple was built “in forty-six years,” naturally understood as over a forty-six-year building period.

verses.greek: ἐκεῖνος δὲ ἔλεγεν περὶ τοῦ ναοῦ τοῦ σώματος αὐτοῦ.
verses.dgt: But he was speaking about the temple of his body.
verses.literal: But that one was speaking concerning the temple of his body.
notes: John explicitly interprets the ναός as Jesus’ body.

verses.greek: ὅτε οὖν ἠγέρθη ἐκ νεκρῶν, ἐμνήσθησαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι τοῦτο ἔλεγεν, καὶ ἐπίστευσαν τῇ γραφῇ καὶ τῷ λόγῳ ὃν εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς.
verses.dgt: Therefore, when he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and they believed the Scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken.
verses.literal: Therefore when he was raised from dead ones, his disciples remembered that this he was saying, and they believed the Scripture and the word which Jesus said.
notes: γραφῇ is singular: “the Scripture.”

verses.greek: Ὡς δὲ ἦν ἐν τοῖς Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐν τῷ πάσχα ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ, πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, θεωροῦντες αὐτοῦ τὰ σημεῖα ἃ ἐποίει·
verses.dgt: Now while he was in Jerusalem at the Passover, during the festival, many believed in his name when they saw the signs he was doing.
verses.literal: And while he was in Jerusalem at the Passover, at the feast, many believed into his name, seeing his signs which he was doing.
notes: πιστεύω is used here for the many who “believed” in Jesus’ name.

verses.greek: αὐτὸς δὲ Ἰησοῦς οὐκ ἐπίστευεν αὑτὸν αὐτοῖς διὰ τὸ αὐτὸν γινώσκειν πάντας
verses.dgt: But Jesus himself did not entrust himself to them, because he knew everyone,
verses.literal: But Jesus himself was not entrusting himself to them, because he knew all people.
notes: The same verb πιστεύω appears again, now meaning Jesus did not “entrust” himself to them, creating a deliberate wordplay.

verses.greek: καὶ ὅτι οὐ χρείαν εἶχεν ἵνα τις μαρτυρήσῃ περὶ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, αὐτὸς γὰρ ἐγίνωσκεν τί ἦν ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ.
verses.dgt: and because he had no need for anyone to testify about a person, for he himself knew what was in a person.
verses.literal: And because he had no need that anyone should testify concerning the person, for he himself knew what was in the person.
notes: γινώσκω (“know”) is repeated across verses 24–25; ἄνθρωπος is generic, so DGT uses “person.”
